disposition_reason: FAAS results for Cu, Fe, Pb, Zn (and non-detects for Cr, Cd, Ni) in 49 grocery foods are printed as category summaries, with a few per-food values in the text.

study.design: Single-purchase grocery survey of 49 foods with a consumption questionnaire (396 participants)
study.market: local grocery store, Greensboro, North Carolina, USA
study.method: Oven drying 55 °C, 6 M HNO3 digestion, flame AAS (Thermo ICE 3000)
study.qa: Blank subtraction, triplicates, repeat purchase after 30 days, spike recovery 80-120% on ten samples; no CRM

unresolved: Per-food concentrations are not tabulated; only category average, maximum and minimum (Tables 3-6) and a few per-food values in the text.
Basis (dry vs fresh) is not labelled in the tables; samples were oven dried before digestion.
Text gives LOQ range 0.4 µg/g for Pb, but Table 2 gives Pb LOQ 0.0422 µg/g.
Table 3 overall min/max values are inconsistent with the category tables (flagged).
Ca and Mg results not recorded (macro minerals).
Lead values around 10 µg/g in all foods are implausibly high for ordinary foods; no CRM was analysed.
